title: The Shifting Drivers of Global Liquidity

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: This Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report (No. 819, June 2017, revised August 2019) examines how the sensitivity of global liquidity components—international loan and bond flows—to global factors varied over the post-crisis decade. The authors find that sensitivity to U.S. monetary policy rose substantially after the global financial crisis, peaked around the 2013 Fed 'taper tantrum,' and then reverted toward pre-crisis levels. Meanwhile, the responsiveness of international bank lending to global risk conditions declined steadily throughout the post-crisis period. The main driver of fluctuations in sensitivity to U.S. monetary policy was the degree of convergence among advanced economy monetary policies, while the post-crisis decline in bank lending sensitivity to risk was driven by increases in lending shares of better-capitalized banking systems.
key_points: Sensitivity of global liquidity components to U.S. monetary policy rose after the GFC, peaked around the 2013 'taper tantrum,' and reverted toward pre-crisis levels thereafter
Responsiveness of international bank lending to global risk conditions declined steadily throughout the post-crisis period
The primary driver of fluctuations in sensitivity to U.S. monetary policy was the degree of convergence among advanced economy monetary policies
The post-crisis decline in sensitivity of international bank lending to global risk was driven by increases in lending shares of better-capitalized banking systems
The study covers JEL classifications F34 (International Lending and Debt Problems), G10 (General Financial Markets), and G21 (Financial Institutions and Services)
The paper is available only in PDF format
why_it_matters: Understanding the shifting drivers of global liquidity is critical for policymakers and market participants because it reveals how transmission mechanisms between U.S. monetary policy and cross-border capital flows have evolved. The finding that advanced economy policy convergence drives the sensitivity of liquidity flows to U.S. policy has direct implications for anticipating market reactions to Fed actions in a multi-polar policy environment.
macro_context: The paper provides macro context by explaining how global liquidity flows respond to U.S. monetary policy and global risk conditions, relevant to understanding capital flow dynamics and cross-border investment patterns.
market_structure_context: The paper is directly relevant to market structure as it examines the mechanics of global liquidity transmission, international bank lending behavior, and the role of banking system capitalization in shaping cross-border capital flows.
